title: Unemployment Benefit Claims Payment Holds and Their Release
content:
An Unemployment Benefit Claims record is placed on hold when an unresolved issue would make payment improper. The hold reason shown on the claim names the issue.

| Hold reason | Issue | Released when |
|---|---|---|
| Nonmonetary issue | An able-and-available, refusal-of-work or separation question awaiting a determination | The determination on the issue is recorded |
| Identity verification | The claim's identity verification case is not verified | Only when the identity verification case linked to the claim has status verified |
| Fraud review | The claim is referred for suspected impostor filing | Only by the fraud unit, never on the claimant's own statement |

## While a hold is in force

- No weekly payment is issued, but the claimant keeps certifying each week.
- Held weeks are paid after the hold is released if they are otherwise payable.

## Release

- Releasing a hold sets the hold reason to none.
- When several issues are open at once the claim stays on hold until the last of them is resolved, and the hold reason shows the issue still open.

## Basis of an identity verification release

The identity verification hold is released only on the record: the Claimant Identity Verification case linked to the claim must show status verified. A case in any other status does not support the release.

### Hypothetical illustration

A claim on hold for identity verification also has a nonmonetary issue open. When the identity verification case shows verified, the claim stays on hold and the hold reason shows the nonmonetary issue still open; held weeks become payable when that issue's determination is recorded, if they are otherwise payable.
